claims.statement: The local-webhook entrypoint is WebhookEngine.sendLocalWebhook(context, sms), called from IncomingMessageDispatcher.dispatch — the single fan-out for inbound SMS/MMS — after the Room shadow mirror (which commits the message AND the durable cloud event in one transaction) and the blocklist check (the dispatcher is the only caller), so webhook dispatch reflects provider-persisted message state, runs exactly once per delivered message (SmsReceiver dedupes SMS_RECEIVED against SMS_DELIVER; MMS arrives once via mmslib's MmsReceiver), and MMS is included through the same path.

Messages from blocked senders never reach the local-webhook entrypoint: IncomingMessageDispatcher returns silently (no bus event, no local webhook, no notification; the row stays persisted) before calling WebhookEngine.sendLocalWebhook — but the Room mirror (which commits the durable cloud event) already ran, so blocked senders are invisible to webhook consumers by construction rather than by receiver-side filtering, and are NOT invisible to the durable outbox.

The local-webhook dispatch is gated by a single check at the WebhookEngine entry — GatewayAccessPolicy.canTransmit(prefs.hasGatewayConsent, prefs.isEnabled), i.e. versioned consent AND the supervisor-derived runtime isEnabled flag — and when it fails the entire local-webhook dispatch is skipped at once with no partial dispatch; the durable cloud event is no longer dispatched from WebhookEngine and is gated/transmitted separately (see EventUploader).

Gateway consent is versioned: hasGatewayConsent is true only when the stored consent version is >= CURRENT_CONSENT_VERSION (currently 1), so material data-use changes force a fresh opt-in before any webhook or cloud event is dispatched.

The local-webhook dispatch is fire-and-forget: it is launched as a single coroutine on WebhookEngine's private CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.IO); the HTTP response code is read only to be logged and exceptions are caught and logged, so a webhook failure can never block or fail the SMS receiver. (The durable cloud event is not dispatched this way — it is committed in the Room transaction and transmitted by EventUploader with retry/ACK.)

The local webhook body is a fixed five-field JSON object: event (always the literal "sms_received"), sender (originating address), message (full body), timestamp (sms.date in Unix epoch milliseconds), and threadId; the schema is WebhookPayload in docs/api/openapi.yaml.

The local webhook URL must start with https://: at dispatch time a non-HTTPS trimmed URL is logged ('Webhook URL rejected — HTTPS required') and never POSTed; a blank URL simply means no local dispatch.

Unlike GatewayPreferences.backendUrl (whose setter requires https:// and throws on plaintext), the webhookUrl setter performs no scheme check, so a non-HTTPS webhook URL can be saved from the UI but is rejected on every dispatch attempt.

When the user-configured webhook signing secret is non-blank, the request carries X-Timestamp (System.currentTimeMillis() as a string) and X-Signature = lowercase hex(HMAC_SHA256(secret, '<X-Timestamp>.<raw-body>')) computed with javax.crypto.Mac over the exact serialized JSON bytes that are POSTed; the timestamp in the signed string enables replay rejection, and docs/api instructs receivers to compare in constant time and reject stale timestamps; with a blank secret the request is sent unsigned with no X-* headers.
The local webhook request is a JSON POST with Content-Type application/json; charset=utf-8, User-Agent Android-SMS-Gateway/<APP_VERSION>, and 8-second connect and 8-second read timeouts.

The durable cloud event path is gated by a different check than the local webhook: EventUploader's loop transmits only while prefs.isEnabled is true AND prefs.gmwebUrl is non-blank — the loop has no explicit consent term (the supervisor only starts the uploader when consent is present) — so while gated it makes zero HTTP and queued events accumulate in the outbox; this supersedes the deleted fire-and-forget leg's gate, which required isRegistered and a non-blank gatewayToken.

The durable cloud event's identity is deterministic and provider-row-derived (replacing the deleted body-derived eventId): GatewayEventFactory derives a stable messageId as UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes of '<source>:<providerId>:<createdAtMs>' (never from body/timestamp alone) and a separate per-event eventUuid as UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes of 'evt:<eventType>:<source>:<providerId>:<dateMs>', so the same message keeps the same messageId across all its events, a rebuilt event dedupes against the outbox unique eventUuid index, and different event kinds for the same row get distinct UUIDs that coexist.

The durable cloud path transmits batches to POST {backend}/api/v1/agent/events/batch through BackendClient, each event carrying eventId (its eventUuid), type, conversationId, encoding, schemaVersion, cryptoVersion, and payload — the base64 envelope bytes sent verbatim (the server treats them as opaque and never parses message content); this replaces the deleted single-event POST /api/gateways/events/sms whose plaintext {eventId, type, sender, message, timestamp} shape no longer appears in code.

The 500-entry sent-event-ID store — hasEventBeenSent, markEventSent, getSentEventIds, the cloud_sent_event_ids key, and MAX_EVENT_IDS=500 — still exists in GatewayPreferences (a JSON array, insertion-ordered, oldest-first FIFO trim, with a corrupt value read back as an empty list), but after PR-02 it has NO callers: it is dead code residue from the deleted fire-and-forget cloud leg and is not part of the live path, which dedupes via the outbox unique eventUuid index instead.

BackendClient.post re-checks that the backend URL starts with https:// before opening any connection (returning Failure 'Insecure backend URL rejected — HTTPS required'), sends Authorization: Bearer <gatewayToken> when authenticated and the token is non-blank, uses 15s connect / 30s read timeouts, and returns a sealed Result<T> (no exceptions leak) with HTTP 401/403 classified as Failure(isAuthError = true).

The webhook signing secret is stored Keystore-encrypted (enc:v1: prefix via SecureStore) with legacy plaintext re-encrypted on first read, and persistence is fail-closed: storeEncrypted throws when the Android Keystore is unavailable instead of degrading to plaintext, so a dead Keystore manifests as an empty/blank secret (unsigned webhook) rather than a plaintext secret leak.

The local webhook is configured on the Gateway screen via GatewayViewModel.saveWebhookUrl (trim + persist to gateway_webhook_url) and saveWebhookSecret (trim + persist; blank value disables signing and logs 'Webhook signing disabled', non-blank enables 'X-Signature' signing); there is no separate on/off toggle — a non-blank URL plus the passing consent/runtime gate is the whole dispatch condition.

revokeGatewayConsent() removes the consent version and accepted-at timestamp, resets isEnabled, gatewayDesiredEnabled, and autoStartOnBoot, and calls clearCloudCredentials() (drops gatewayId, gatewayToken, isRegistered); the local webhook stops immediately, and because isEnabled is reset the uploader loop gate (isEnabled && gmwebUrl) closes at once, so queued outbox events stay PENDING (durable, retriable) and the legs cannot resurrect after a reboot.

MMS messages flow through the same webhook path: MmsReceiver reads the persisted Mms row and calls IncomingMessageDispatcher.dispatch with source = SOURCE_MMS, so the webhook message field for MMS is the text/plain part body, falling back to the subject, then the literal '[MMS]' placeholder.

The webhook and cloud-event contracts are published in docs/api/README.md and docs/api/openapi.yaml (the /webhooks/sms.received endpoint doc, the IncomingSmsWebhook callback, the WebhookPayload schema, signature-verification guidance, and x-cloud-backend-contract for the cloud backend endpoints) as the shareable spec for webhook receivers and relay-backend implementers, with the versioning rule that openapi.yaml must be updated in the same PR as any endpoint change; note the x-cloud-backend-contract still documents the legacy POST /api/gateways/events/sms endpoint, which no in-repo client calls — the live durable path posts to /api/v1/agent/events/batch instead.

GatewayAccessPolicyTest unit-tests the canStart/canTransmit truth tables the local webhook is gated on (run via ./gradlew test); the durable path is additionally pinned in-repo by GatewayEventFactoryTest (stable messageId, per-kind eventUuid, envelope round-trip, cryptoVersion=1 rejection), GatewaySyncPolicyTest (100-event/512 KiB batch caps, lone oversized event, full-jitter backoff bounds), and GatewaySyncSchemaTest (MIGRATION_6_7 additive-only, UNIQUE eventUuid index). WebhookEngine, BackendClient, and GatewayPreferences are Android-dependent (HttpURLConnection, SharedPreferences, Keystore) with no in-repo JVM tests, observed on-device via logcat (WEBHOOK_ENGINE, BACKEND_CLIENT, EVENT_UPLOADER tags) and the gateway screen log flow.

The in-repo live smoke script scripts/test-gateway-api.ps1 (referenced from the docs/api tests section) exercises the device's LAN REST API — status probe, auth rejection (401), send SMS, inbox, and filtered query — rather than the inbound webhook or cloud-event upload path, so it does not verify either outbound notification leg.

For a newly-landed message, TelephonySyncCoordinator.mutate(Upsert) commits the matching durable cloud event inside the SAME Room transaction as the message + conversation upsert: when the message row is new (old == null) it calls enqueueCloudEvent { GatewayEventFactory.messageCreated(...) }, which insertOrIgnore's the row on the unique eventUuid — so the event and message rows live or die together (a process death loses both and the provider reconcile re-mirrors and re-enqueues), a re-commit of the same event is a no-op rather than a duplicate, and a failed enqueue is caught and logged without failing the local mutation.

EventUploader is the sole durable cloud transmitter: it is instantiated in GatewayService.onCreate and driven by ConnectionSupervisor (started when the gateway comes online alongside the heartbeat/pollers; stopped when consent is absent, the runtime is disabled, the network drops, or on shutdown), and it owns no RAM-only state — the gateway_event_outbox is the source of truth, so it drains the durable path independently of the local webhook.

EventUploader's loop recovers first (on start it calls recoverSending() to requeue any SENDING rows a crash left between claim and ACK), then per batch: claimBatch (transactional → SENDING, capped at 100 events / 512 KiB) → POST the batch → on Success parse accepted[] for per-eventUuid partial ACK (reported → ACKED, missing → PENDING + backoff); a transport failure or 429 requeues the batch with full-jitter exponential backoff (2 s base, 5 min cap), a permanent 4xx (400–499 excluding 429) dead-letters the whole batch, and an undecodable envelope dead-letters that single row only; DEAD_LETTER is a visible state, never a silent drop.

Durable cloud events keep PII out of the envelope: each outbox row stores sender/body only inside the payload bytes as an envelope.v1 JSON of {ciphertextB64, encoding, schemaVersion, cryptoVersion} (cryptoVersion=0 means UTF-8 JSON plaintext in PR-02), and GatewayEventFactory.decodePayloadEnvelope rejects any cryptoVersion != 0 — the Phase 7 (ADR-002) AEAD extension point that must not change the factory's public shape.
